IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r1.claim: The transition from shadow and daylight to night and day is apt because night resembles shadow: darkness follows the sun’s light.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r1.anchor: مناسبة الانتقال من الاستدلال باعتبار أحوال الظل والضحاء إلى الاعتبار بأحوال الليل والنهار ظاهرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r2.claim: The defined parts of the clause indicate exclusive agency: only God makes night and day; Quraysh acknowledged His creation but their partners cannot share divine control, which cannot be divided.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r2.anchor: ومورد الاستدلال المقصد المستفاد من تعريف جزأي الجملة وهو قصر إفراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r3.claim: Lakum attaches to jaʿala and names one benefit, not the only purpose; night results when the turning earth’s side is hidden from the sun and serves many ends, including 25:62.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r3.anchor: و { لكم } متعلق ب { جعل } أي من جملة ما خلق له الليل أنه يكون لباسا لكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r4.claim: The discourse shifts from first person to third person as an instance of iltifāt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r4.anchor: وقد رجع أسلوب الكلام من المتكلم إلى الغيبة على طريقة الالتفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r5.claim: Night is a direct metaphor as clothing that conceals people from one another, providing many benefits for private needs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r5.anchor: و { لباسا } مشبه به على طريقة التشبيه البليغ ، أي ساترا لكم يستر بعضكم عن بعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r6.claim: Mentioning night’s concealment before sleep suits the link between night and shadow; 78:8–10 orders sleep first because it matters more and connects more closely with creating spouses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r6.anchor: وتقديم الاعتبار بحالة ستر الليل على الاعتبار بحالة النوم لرعي مناسبة الليل بالظل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r7.claim: The verse both argues and reminds: night-day alternation demonstrates the precise systems of earth’s rotation and sunlight, while night supports rest, renewed vigor, concealment, and day supports work and sight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p44/r7.anchor: وقد جمعت الآية استدلالا وامتنانا فهي دليل على عظم قدرة الخالق

STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.claim: A minority classifies most of the surah as Madinan but verses 68–70 as Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.anchor: while a minority consider most of the sūrah to be from the Madinan period and vv. 68–70 to be from the Makkan period

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r3.claim: Daytime rising recalls resurrection after death, and the word nushur eloquently points to the afterlife.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r3.anchor: they will also one day awake from the sleep of death on the Day of Judgement

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r4.claim: Night and day display providence, mercy, power, wisdom, monotheism, and the hereafter; they prove Qur’anic claims to those willing to reflect, a theme revisited in 25:82-87.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p383/r4.anchor: All these signs are sufficient to prove every statement of the Qur’ ān

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r1.claim: Night is likened to clothing because it covers and conceals things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r1.anchor: جعل لكم الليل لباسا تشبيها بالثوب الذي يغطي البدن ويستره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya describes subat as a coma affecting an awake person through illness and thus compares sleep to it; السبت means remaining in place, so subat is complete stillness, while nushur as revival parallels sleep’s death with waking’s life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r2.anchor: والسبات: ضرب من الإغماء يعتري اليقظان مرضا فشبه النوم به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r3.speaker: غيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r3.claim: Another explanation takes subat as rest: sleep is called that because it produces rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r3.anchor: وقال غيره: السبات الراحة جعل النوم سباتا أي سبب راحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says subat means death, citing 6:60; he rejects rest because nushur is opposite it, though Abū Ḥayyān says this objection works only if nushur must mean life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: السبات الموت وهو كقوله وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r5.claim: Abu Muslim interprets nushur as spreading out and movement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r5.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم نشورا هو بمعنى الانتشار والحركة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya suggests nushur may mean the time of going out and dispersing to seek livelihood and God’s bounty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بالنشور وقت انتشار وتفرق لطلب المعاش وابتغاء فضل الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r7.claim: The night and day imagery pairs a sleeping night with a fasting day; besides proving divine power, night’s veil benefits people religiously and in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق فيها إظهار لنعمته على خلقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r8.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r8.claim: An unnamed poet says night’s darkness has offered him many favors, as evidence against Manichaean dualism.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r8.anchor:
وقال الشاعر:
وكم لظلام الليل عندي من يد ... تخبر أن المانوية تكذب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r9.speaker: لقمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r9.claim: Luqman tells his son that waking after sleep illustrates how people will be raised after death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p114/r9.anchor: وعن لقمان أنه قال لابنه: يا بني كما تنام فتوقظ فكذلك تموت فتنشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r7.claim: Night covers everything like clothing; sleep rests bodies and cuts off work, from a root meaning to cut.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r7.anchor: الليل لباسا} أي: سترا تستترون به، يريد أن ظلمته تغشى كل شيء، كاللباس الذي يشتمل على لابسه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r8.claim: Day is waking and the time when people spread out to seek livelihood and attend their tasks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r8.anchor: {وجعل النهار نشورا} أي: يقظة وزمانا، تنتشرون فيه لابتغاء الرزق، وتنتشرون لأشغالكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r12.claim: The sleeper is called masbūt because his work and movement have stopped.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r12.anchor: والنائم مسبوت لأنه انقطع عمله وحركته.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r7.claim: Night covers people, sleep rests their bodies, and daytime lets them spread out after sleep.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r7.anchor: النوم سباتا } راحة لأبدانكم { وجعل النهار نشورا } حياة تنتشرون فيه من النوم.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r1.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r1.claim: Al-Jurjānī argues that subtle rhetorical merits are hidden and spiritual, and recognition requires receptive nature, taste, and critical instinct.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r1.anchor: المزايا التي تحتاج أن تُعلمهم مكانها وتصور لهم شأنها، أمور خفية ومعان روحانية، أنت لا تستطيع أن تنبه السامع لها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r2.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r2.claim: He demonstrates rhetorical distinctions through poetic examples by al-Buḥturī, Abū Nuwās, and Ismāʿīl ibn Yasār, rather than Qur'anic citations.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p126/r2.anchor: ولاحظ أن الجرحاني على منهجه في الدلائل في الاستكشار من الشواهد الشعرية، لا القرآنية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r1.claim: The night as covering is one of God's wonderful signs of power and abundant mercy; addressing people directly gives the expression its full force as a reminder of favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r1.anchor: بيان لبعض بدائع آثار قدرته عز وجل وروائع أحكام رحمته ونعمته الفائضة على الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r2.claim: The beneficiary phrase is attached to جعل and placed before its two objects to foreground that the following benefits are for people; the transition from shadow to night, the earth's shadow, is especially graceful.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r2.anchor: واللام متعلقة بجعل وتقديمها على مفعوليه للاعتناء ببيان كون ما بعد من منافعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r3.claim: Night covers people with darkness as clothing covers them.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r3.anchor: جعل لنفعكم الليل كاللباس يستركم بظلامه كما يستركم اللباس

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r4.claim: Sleep usually occurs when vapors overpower the faculties; the proposed cause of sleep as a breeze from beneath the Throne is scarcely sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r4.anchor: بسبب استيلاء الأبخرة على القوى عادة وقيل : بشم نسيم يهب من تحت العرش ولا يكاد يصح

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r5.claim: As repose for bodies, sleep cuts off the activities of wakefulness; the root sense of sabt is cutting.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r5.anchor: راحة للابدان بقطع الأفاعيل التي تكون حال اليقظة وأصل السبت القطع

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r6.claim: Other explanations connect sabt with the Sabbath's customary rest, the claim that God created nothing that day, or the term for a patient resting from illness; Abu Muslim adopts the last usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r6.anchor: ويقال للعليل إذا استراح من تعب العلة : مسبوت وإلى هذا ذهب أبو مسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan describes sabat as a kind of faint that can afflict an awake person in illness, making sleep analogous to it; sabt can also mean staying in one place, like sleep's stillness.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : السبات ضرب من الأغماء يعتري اليقظان مرضا فشبه النوم به

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r8.claim: Daytime is when people spread out to seek their livelihood, comparable to 78:11.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r8.anchor: ينتشر فيه الناس لطلب المعاش فهو كقوله تعالى : ( وجعلنا النهار معاشا )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r9.claim: Calling day itself nushur, rather than merely a time for it, intensifies the expression; it can also be an active participle, with the action attributed figuratively to the day.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r9.anchor: وفي جعله نفس النشور مبالغة وقيل : نشورا بمعنى ناشرا على الاسناد المجازي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r10.claim: Another reading takes sleep as death because both cut off sensation, and daytime as resurrection from that repose, or resurrection itself; 6:60 and 39:42 compare sleep with death.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالسبات الموت لما فيه من قطع الاحساس أو الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects repose as the meaning of sabat because it clashes with nushur in the parallel phrase; he takes nushur as resurrection, since Quranic usage rarely means ordinary spreading for work.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r11.anchor: وأبى الزمخشري الراحة في تفسير السبات وقال : انه يأباه النشور في مقابلته

ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r12.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r12.claim: Al-Kashf supports linking nushur to resurrection: the surrounding verses combine reminders of blessing and power with evidence for return, as do the parallel verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p28#2/r12.anchor: الآيات السابقة واللاحقة مع ما فيها من التذكير بالنعمة والقدرة أدمج فيها الدلالة على الاعادة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p29/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p29/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p29/r1.claim: Night's covering together with sleep as repose forms a single contrast to daytime activity; repeating جعل suits nushur's sense of visible emergence and strenuous movement, or resurrection. Sura 78 phrases the pair differently.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p29/r1.anchor: جعل الليل لباسا والنوم فيه سباتا بمجموعه مقابل جعل النهار نشورا ولهذا كرر جعل فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r1.claim: Night's darkness is likened to clothing because it covers people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r2.claim: Sleep is rest because it cuts off occupations, or death, as in 6:60, because it cuts life; al-masbūt means dead.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r2.anchor: راحة للأبدان بقطع المشاغل، وأصل السبت القطع أو موتا

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r3.claim: The day is spreading forth for livelihood, or rising from sleep analogous to resurrection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r3.anchor: ذا نشور أي انتشار ينتشر فيه الناس للمعاش

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r4.claim: Sleep and waking foreshadow death and resurrection.

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r5.speaker: لقمان
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r5.claim: Luqmān tells his son that waking after sleep is like being raised after death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:47-48/r5.anchor: يا بني كما تنام فتوقظ كذلك تموت فتنشر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r1.claim: After the preceding sign involving shadow, this verse names night and day to make the proof of God and His favor to creation explicit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r1.anchor: ولما تضمنت هذه الآية الليل النهار , قال مصرحا بهما دليلا على الحق , وإظهارا للنعمة على الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r2.claim: Night is like clothing because it conceals things from sight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r2.anchor: { لباسا } اي ساترا للأشياء عن الأبصار كما يستر اللباس { والنوم سباتا }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r3.claim: Subāt is sleep, stillness, and rest; its root carries the sense of cutting off.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r3.anchor: قال البغوي وغيره : وأصل السبت القطع . وفي جعله سبحانه كذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r4.claim: Sleep is a minor death that suspends sensation and awareness, making death evident to people of insight; its religious and worldly benefits are countless.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r4.anchor: { والنوم سباتا } أي نوما وسكونا وراحة , عبارة عن كونه موتا أصغر طاويا لما كان من الإحساس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r5.claim: Daytime is renewed life, movement, and activity: waking restores the senses sleep had suspended and recalls resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r5.anchor: { وجعل النهار نشورا * } أي حياة وحركة وتقلبا بما أوجد فيه من اليقظة المذكرة بالبعث ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r6.speaker: لقمان
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r6.claim: Luqmān tells his son that being awakened after sleep resembles being raised after death.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r6.anchor: قال لابنه : كما تنام فتوقظ فكذلك تموت فتنشر .

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r7.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by reciprocal implication: mentioning rest first implies later movement, while mentioning resurrection second implies prior stillness and sleep.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r7.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر السبات أولا دليلا على الحركة ثانيا , والنشور ثانيا دليلا على الطي والكسون أولا .

BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r8.claim: After showing God’s power over meanings through creation, removal, death, and life, Biqāʿī turns to visible things and more distant causes of death and life.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p324/r8.anchor: ولما دل على عظمته بتصرفه في المعاني بالإيجاد والإعدام , وختمه بالإماتة والإحياء بأسباب قريبة , أتبعه التصرف في الأعيان

DURR-FULL:v6p262/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas divides daylight into twelve hours, describing its progression from dawn through the morning, noon, afternoon, and final hours before night; he associates noon prayer with the sun’s decline.
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r2.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس قال: إن النهار اثنتا عشرة ساعة فأول الساعة ما بين طلوع الفجر إلى أن ترى شعاع الشمس

DURR-FULL:v6p262/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses the day as the time in which people spread out.
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله وجعل النهار نشورا {وجعل النهار نشورا} قال: ينشر فيه

DURR-FULL:v6p262/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r4.claim: Qatāda says daylight is for people’s livelihoods, needs, and movement about their affairs.
DURR-FULL:v6p262/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {وجعل النهار نشورا} قال: لمعايشهم وحوائجهم وتصرفهم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses the daytime as a time of spreading out.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : النهار نشورا ينشر فيه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r2.claim: Qatāda says daytime is made for people’s livelihoods, needs, and movement.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2704/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا والنهار نشورا لمعايشهم ولحوائجهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p39/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p39/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p39/r3.claim: The metaphor makes guidance like sunlight and the shrinking of unbelief’s darkness like a long shadow contracting after sunrise; this explains the link to the day’s resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p39/r3.anchor: وبهذه النكتة عطف قوله { ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا }

BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r1.claim: God makes night cover people with darkness like clothing; labs means covering, and the Qur’an similarly calls spouses garments for each other and piety a garment by analogy.
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r1.anchor: كاللباس يستركم بظلامه كما يستر اللباس فشبه ظلامه باللباس في الستر وأصل اللبس ستر الشيء

BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r2.claim: Night’s darkness does not remove the prayer requirement to cover one’s nakedness; that requirement remains in darkness and light.
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r2.anchor: لا اعتبار لستر الظلمة فإن ستر العورة باللباس ونحوه لحق الصلاة وهو باق في الظلمة والضوء

BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r3.claim: Sleep is relaxation of the brain’s nerves due to rising moist vapor; sabt means stopping work, and Saturday is named for that stoppage, or for ending the days after six days of creation.
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r3.anchor: النوم استرخاء أعصاب الدماغ برطوبات البخار الصاعد والسبت قطع العمل ويوم سبتهم يوم قطعهم للعمل

BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r4.claim: Sleep, usually at night, rests the body by interrupting waking occupations; alternatively, sleep is called death because both share a severing of life, as 6:60 says God takes people at night.
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r4.anchor: وجعل النوم الذي يقع في الليل غالبا راحة للأبدان بقطع المشاغل والأعمال المختصة بحال اليقظة أو جعله موتا

BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r5.claim: Death wholly separates the spirit’s light from the body, while sleep separates it only from the body’s exterior, not its interior; masbut can mean dead or unconscious, so such patients should not be buried before a day and night confirms death.
BURSEVI:v6p160#3/r5.anchor: أن الموت هو الانقطاع الكلي أي انقطاع ضوء الروح عن ظاهر البدن وباطنه

BURSEVI:v6p161/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p161/r1.claim: Daytime is when light spreads; legally it runs from dawn to sunset, though its basic sense runs from sunrise to sunset.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r1.anchor: النهار الوقت الذي ينتشر فيه الضوء وهو في الشرع ما بين طلوع الفجر إلى غروب الشمس وفي الأصل ما بين طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها

BURSEVI:v6p161/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p161/r2.claim: Nushūr can mean spreading: daylight is when people spread out to seek their livelihood, as in 28:73.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r2.anchor: أي وجعل النهار ذا نشور أي انتشار ينتشر فيه الناس لطلب المعاش وابتغاء الرزق

BURSEVI:v6p161/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p161/r3.claim: Alternatively, nushūr means resurrection: daylight is rising from sleep, which models the raising of the dead.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r3.anchor: أو من نشر الميت إذا عاد حيا أي وجعل النهار زمام بعث من ذلك السبات والنوم كبعث الموتى

BURSEVI:v6p161/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p161/r4.claim: On the resurrection reading, the phrase omits a genitive and substitutes its complement, intensifying the identification with resurrection itself.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r4.anchor: على حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه أي نفس البعث على الطريق المبالغة

BURSEVI:v6p161/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p161/r5.claim: Sleep and waking are inward models of death and resurrection.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r5.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن النوم واليقظة انموذج للموت والنشور

BURSEVI:v6p161/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r6.speaker: لقمان عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p161/r6.claim: Luqman tells his son that being awakened after sleep resembles dying and then being resurrected.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r6.anchor: وعن لقمان عليه السلام : يا بني كما تنام فتوقظ كذلك تموت فتنشر

BURSEVI:v6p161/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r7.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p161/r7.claim: The Mathnawi couplet likewise compares sleep with death.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r7.anchor: نوم ما ون شد اخ الموت أي فلان زين برادر آن برادرا بدان

BURSEVI:v6p161/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p161/r8.claim: The verse permits sleep only to the extent needed to relieve bodily fatigue.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r8.anchor: وفي الآية رخصة للمنام بقدر دفع الضرورة وهو فتور البدن

BURSEVI:v6p161/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r9.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p161/r9.claim: Some spiritual elders say sleep rests the body, whereas spiritual disciplines tire it, so the two are opposed.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r9.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : النوم راحة للبدن والمجاهدات إتعاب البدن فيتضادان

BURSEVI:v6p161/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r10.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p161/r10.claim: Sleep closes the outward senses so the senses of the heart can open.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r10.anchor: وحقيقة النوم سد حواس الظاهر لفتح حواس القلب

BURSEVI:v6p161/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r11.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p161/r11.claim: The holy spirit, divine subtlety, or rational soul is a stranger imprisoned in the low body and occupied with maintaining it while one is awake.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r11.anchor: الحكمة في النوم أن الروح القدسي أو اللطيفة الربانية أو النفس الناطقة غريبة جدا في هذا الجسم السفلي

BURSEVI:v6p161/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r12.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p161/r12.claim: In sleep the spirit returns to its original abode and rests among spirits, receiving unseen meanings represented through images in the visible world; this underlies dream interpretation.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r12.anchor: فإذا نام ذهب إلى مكانه الأصلي ومعدنه الذاتي فيستريح بواسطة لقاء الأوراح ومعرفة المعاني والغيوب

BURSEVI:v6p161/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r13.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p161/r13.claim: When a spiritual striver abandons sleep and rest, the four elements dissolve and the heart is unveiled to see the dominion of spirits and long for God.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r13.anchor: عليه أجزاء الأركان الأربعة من الترابية والمائية والنارية والهوائية فيعرى القلب حينئذ عن الحجب

BURSEVI:v6p161/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p161/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p161/r14.claim: Shah Shuja is said to have avoided sleep for thirty years, then seen God in a dream one night and thereafter carried a pillow and lay down wherever he went.
BURSEVI:v6p161/r14.anchor: كما حكي عن شاه شجاع أنه لم ينم ثلاثين سنة فاتفق أنه نام ليلة فرأى الحق سبحانه في منامه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r11.claim: Al-Tabari says night is called clothing because it covers and envelops things.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r11.anchor: قال الطبري ووصف الليل باللباس تشبيها من حيث يستر الأشياء ويغشاها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r12.claim: Sabat is a swoon that illness can cause in an awake person, and sleep is likened to it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r12.anchor: ضرب من الإغماء يعتري اليقظان مرضا، فشبه النائم به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r13.claim: Since sabt can mean staying in one place, sabat also suggests stillness and settled repose.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r13.anchor: والسبت الإقامة في المكان فكأن السبات سكون ما وثبوت عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r14.claim: Nushur can mean revival: waking is likened to resurrection, matching death and taking of the soul implicit in sleep.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r14.anchor: في هذا الموضع الإحياء شبه اليقظة به ليتطابق الإحياء مع الإماتة والتوفي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r15.claim: Alternatively, nushur is when people disperse to seek livelihoods and God's bounty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r15.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد ب «النشور» وقت انتشار وتفرق لطلب المعايش وابتغاء فضل الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r16.claim: The wording pairs a sleeping night with a fasting day, an expression of night sleeping and day fasting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p212#2/r16.anchor: وقوله النهار نشورا وما قبله من باب ليل نائم ونهار صائم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r1.claim: Night is clothing because its darkness covers and envelops people as clothes envelop the wearer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r1.anchor: أي ساترا بظلمته لأن ظلمته تغشى الاشخاص وتشتمل عليها اشتمال اللباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says subāt means rest; Saturday was named for rest after creation was completed on Friday and the Israelites were told to rest.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي راحة ومنه يوم السبت لأن الخلق اجتمع يوم الجمعة وكان الفراغ منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba also derives sabt from stretching out: whoever stretches out rests.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r3.anchor: وأصل السبت التمدد ومن تمدد استراح وقال ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari derives sabt from cutting off, so sleep cuts off one's activities.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري أصل السبت القطع فالمعنى وجعلنا النوم قطعا لأعمالكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says people spread out in daylight seeking provision.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r5.anchor: أحدهما تنتشرون فيه لابتغاء الرزق قاله ابن عباس والثاني تنشر الروح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi says the soul is spread out by waking just as it is spread out at resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p93#3/r6.anchor: والثاني تنشر الروح باليقظة كما تنشر بالبعث حكاه الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114/r6.claim: Night is a garment that envelops existence, as in 92:1 and 91:4.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114/r7.claim: Subāt is cessation of movement for bodily rest: daytime activity tires the limbs, then nighttime stillness brings sleep that rests both body and spirit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114/r7.anchor: أي: قطعا للحركة لراحة الأبدان، فإن الأعضاء والجوارح تكل من كثرة الحركة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p114#2/r1.claim: Nushūr means people spread out in daylight for their livelihoods, earnings, and other needs; Ibn Kathir links this to 28:73.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r1.claim: Night’s darkness is compared to a covering garment because it conceals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r1.anchor: شبه ما يستر من ظلام الليل باللباس الساتر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r2.claim: Subāt means death; one asleep is called masbūt because life is cut off, as in 6:60.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r2.anchor: والسبات : الموت . والمسبوت : الميت ؛ لأنه مقطوع الحياة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r3.claim: He rejects taking subāt to mean rest because the parallel nushūr, awakening or resurrection, rules it out.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r3.anchor: فإن قلت : هلا فسرته بالراحة ؟ قلت : النشور في مقابلته يأباه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r4.claim: The verse demonstrates the Creator’s power and bounty: the night’s concealment has many religious and worldly benefits.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق فيها إظهار لنعمته على خلقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r5.claim: Sleep and wakefulness resemble death and life and provide a lesson to anyone who reflects.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r5.anchor: والنوم واليقظة وشبههما بالموت والحياة ، أي عبرة فيها لمن اعتبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r6.speaker: لقمان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r6.claim: Luqmān tells his son that, just as one sleeps and is awakened, one dies and is raised again.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p288#2/r6.anchor: وعن لقمان أنه قال لابنه : يا بني ، كما تنام فتوقظ

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r12.claim: Night is a covering because it conceals as clothing does.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r12.anchor: يعني غطاء لأن يستر كما يستر اللباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r13.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r13.claim: Al-Naqqash links subat to being cut off: the sleeper does not reason and is like the dead.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r13.anchor: أحدهما : لأنه مسبوت فيه , والنائم لا يعقل كالميت ، حكاه النقاش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r14.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿIsa interprets sleep as rest from stopping work; the Sabbath is named for a day of rest that stops labor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r14.anchor: الثاني : يعني راحة لقطع العمل ومنه سمي يوم السب ، لأنه يوم راحة لقطع العمل , حكاه ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r15.claim: One explanation is that the soul spreads through waking, with nushur echoing spreading and resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r15.anchor: أحدهما : لانتشار الروح باليقظة فيه مأخوذ من النشر والبعث .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r16.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r16.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say daytime is for people to disperse in pursuit of livelihoods.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p146#2/r16.anchor: الثاني : لانتشار الناس في معايشهم ، قاله مجاهد ، وقتادة .

MUJAHID:v2p454#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p454#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p454#2/r1.claim: People spread out during the day.
MUJAHID:v2p454#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وجعل النهار نشورا ﴾ قال ينتشرون فيه

MUQATIL:25:45-49/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r5.claim: Night as a garment means a time of rest.
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r5.anchor: وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا } يعنى سكنا

MUQATIL:25:45-49/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r6.claim: Subāt means that a person is rendered unconscious, as if dead.
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r6.anchor: والنوم سباتا } يعنى الإنسان مسبوتا لا يعقل كأنه ميت

MUQATIL:25:45-49/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r7.claim: In daytime people spread out to seek provision.
MUQATIL:25:45-49/r7.anchor: وجعل النهار نشورا } [آية: 47] ينتشرون فيه لابتغاء الرزق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r1.claim: Night's covering darkness is like a garment.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r2.claim: Sleep rests bodies and cuts off activity; sabat means cutting, and sleepers are called cut off because work and movement cease.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r2.anchor: راحة لأبدانكم وقطعا لأعمالكم والسبت القطع والنائم مسبوت لأنه انقطع عمله وحركته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r3.claim: Another view takes sabat as death: the sleeper is cut off from life, supported by the verse about God taking people at night.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r3.anchor: وقيل السبات الموت المسبوت الميت لأنه مقطوع الحياة وهو كقوله تعالى وهو الذى يتوفاكم بالليل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r4.claim: Day is a resurrection from sleep, when creatures are raised for livelihood, paralleling the raising of the dead.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r4.anchor: إذا لنشور انبعاث من النوم كنشور الميت أى ينشر فيه الخلق للمعاش

NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r5.claim: The verse displays the Creator's power and grace; life is a lesson to anyone who reflects.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق فيها اظهار لنعمته والحياة عبرة لمن اعتبر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r6.speaker: لقمان
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r6.claim: Luqman told his son that sleep should remind one of death, just as death will be followed by resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p171#3/r6.anchor: وقال لقمان لابنه كما تنام فتوعظ كذلك تموت فتنشر

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r1.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains night as a garment by analogy: it covers and envelops things, hiding them.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r1.anchor: قال الطبري: وصف الليل باللباس تشبيها من حيث يستر الأشياء ويغشاها.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī rejects the claim that praying naked in darkness is valid because night covers the body; covering in prayer is worship, not a concession based on being unseen.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r2.anchor: والستر في الصلاة عبادة تختص بها ليست لأجل نظر الناس.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r3.claim: Sleep is rest for the body because it interrupts engagement in activities.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r3.anchor: أي راحة لأبدانكم بانقطاعكم عن الأشغال.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r4.claim: One derivation connects sabāt to stretching: a woman who lets down her hair is said to sabatat it, and a lank-bodied man is masbūt.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r4.anchor: وأصل السبات من التمدد. يقال: سبتت المرأة شعرها أي نقضته وأرسلته. ورجل مسبوت أي ممدود الخلقة.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r5.claim: On this derivation, sleep is called sabāt because stretching involves rest.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r5.anchor: وقيل: للنوم سبات لأنه بالتمدد يكون، وفي التمدد معنى الراحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r6.claim: Another derivation takes sabt as cutting off: sleep cuts people off from work, like the Jews' Sabbath interruption of labor.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r6.anchor: وقيل: السبت القطع فالنوم انقطاع عن الاشتغال ومنه سبت اليهود لانقطاعهم عن الأعمال فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r7.claim: A further gloss takes sabt as remaining in place; sleep is stillness from disturbance and movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r7.anchor: وقيل: السبت الإقامة في المكان فكأن السبات سكون ما وثبوت عليه فالنوم سبات على معنى أنه سكون عن الاضطراب والحركة.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r8.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r8.claim: Al-Khalīl says sabāt is deep sleep, made heavy so the body can recover and rest fully.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r8.anchor: وقال الخليل: السبات نوم ثقيل أي جعلنا نومكم ثقيلا ليكمل الإجمام والراحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r9.claim: Nushūr is daytime spreading for livelihood; day enables people to go about, as waking parallels revival after death.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r9.anchor: من الانتشار للمعاش أي النهار سبب الإحياء للانتشار. شبه اليقظة فيه بتطابق الإحياء مع الإماتة.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r10.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r10.claim: The Prophet would say on waking: praise belongs to God who gave us life after death, and to Him is the resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:47/r10.anchor: وكان عليه السلام إذا أصبح قال: «الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا وإليه النشور».

QASHANI:25:47-49/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:47-49/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:47-49/r1.claim: Night is the soul's darkness, a garment that envelops people and veils them from witnessing the Real, its attributes, and Essence during worldly heedlessness.
QASHANI:25:47-49/r1.anchor: ليل ظلمة النفس { لباسا } يغشاكم بالاستيلاء عن مشاهدة الحق وصفاته والذات وظلالها

QASHANI:25:47-49/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:47-49/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:47-49/r2.claim: Sleep signifies being cut off from everlasting true life.
QASHANI:25:47-49/r2.anchor: تسبتون بها عن الحياة الحقيقية السرمدية كما قال عليه السلام

QASHANI:25:47-49/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:47-49/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:25:47-49/r3.claim: The Prophet says people are asleep and awaken when they die.
QASHANI:25:47-49/r3.anchor: قال عليه السلام: " الناس نيام فإذا ماتوا انتبهوا "

QASHANI:25:47-49/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:47-49/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:47-49/r4.claim: Day is the light of the spirit; it revives hearts, which spread into the space of holiness after sensory sleep.
QASHANI:25:47-49/r4.anchor: نهار نور الروح { نشورا } تحيا قلوبكم به فتنتشرون في فضاء القدس بعد نوم الحس

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r1.claim: Night is likened to clothing because it covers and conceals everything.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r1.anchor: شبه الليل من حيث إنه يستر الكل ويغطي باللباس الساتر للبدن

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r2.claim: Sleep is called subāt because it causes rest; Abū Muslim likewise defines subāt as rest.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r2.anchor: والسبات هو الراحة وجعل النوم سباتا لأنه سبب للراحة

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r3.claim: Abū Muslim relates the name Saturday to customary rest on that day and calls a sick person relieved from illness masbūt.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : السبات الراحة ومنه يوم السبت لما جرت به العادة من الاستراحة فيه ، ويقال للعليل إذا استراح من تعب العلة مسبوت

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r4.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf takes subāt as death and masbūt as dead because life has been cut off; he compares it with 6:60.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r4.anchor: وقال صاحب ( الكشاف ) السبات الموت والمسبوت الميت لأنه مقطوع الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers “death” to “rest” because the following word, nushūr, is its opposite.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r5.anchor: وإنما قلنا إن تفسيره بالموت أولى من تفسيره بالراحة

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r6.claim: Abū Muslim explains daytime nushūr as spreading out and activity.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r6.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : وجعل النهار نشورا } هو بمعنى الانتشار والحركة

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r7.claim: The Qur’an calls sleep a taking of souls, linking waking from sleep with rising from death; 39:42 describes this taking.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r7.anchor: كما سمى تعالى نوم الإنسان وفاة ، فقال : { الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها }

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r8.speaker: لقمان
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r8.claim: Luqmān told his son that just as one sleeps and is awakened, one dies and is resurrected.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r8.anchor: وعن لقمان أنه قال لابنه : كما تنام فتوقظ

RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r9.claim: The alternation displays the Creator’s power and blessings: night’s concealment serves many religious and worldly needs.
RAZI-FULL:v24p78/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق فيها إظهار لنعمه على خلقه

STUDYQURAN:25:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r1.claim: Some cite the proverb that sleep is the brother of death when explaining waking as resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r1.anchor: some mention the proverb, “Sleep is the brother of death”

STUDYQURAN:25:47/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r2.claim: Sleep is associated with death in 6:60 and 39:42, which says God takes souls both at death and during sleep.
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r2.anchor: Sleep is also associated with death in 6:60: He it is Who takes your souls by night, and also 39:42

STUDYQURAN:25:47/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r3.claim: Night, sleep, and day are described in similar language in 78:9–11.
STUDYQURAN:25:47/r3.anchor: The night, sleep, and day are described using similar language in 78:9–11.

QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r2.claim: Night is rest for the heedless, but lovers stay awake: in union, intimacy prevents sleep, and in separation, distress does so; their vigil reflects joy or grief.
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r2.anchor: جعل الليل وقتا لسكون قوم ووقتا لانزعاج آخرين ؛ فأرباب الغفلة يسكنون في ليلهم ، والمحبون يسهرون في ليلهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r3.claim: It is said that lovers may experience in sleep a theophany unavailable while awake, and so prefer sleep to vigil.
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r3.anchor: ويقال جعل النوم للأحباب وقت التجلي بما لا سبيل إليه في اليقظة ، فإذا رأوا ربهم في المنام يؤثرون النوم على السهر

QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r4.speaker: قال قائلهم
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r4.claim: An anonymous lover says he seeks sleep without being drowsy, hoping for a dream in which he meets his beloved.
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r4.anchor: قال قائلهم : وإني لأستغفي وما بي نعسة . . . لعل خيالا منك يلقى خياليا

QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r5.speaker: قال قائلهم
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r5.claim: Another anonymous lover says that seeing his heart’s joy in a dream made him love drowsing and sleep.
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r5.anchor: وقال قائلهم : رأيت سرور قلبي في منامي . . . فأحببت التنعس والمناما

QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r6.claim: Sleep is punishment for the heedless but mercy for the diligent, since God makes them sleep to rest their souls from the strain of spiritual striving.
QUSHAYRI:v2p386/r6.anchor: ويقال النوم لأهل الغفلة عقوبة ولأهل الاجتهاد رحمة

TAB-FULL:v17p466/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p466/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p466/r1.claim: Night is a covering and shelter in which people hide and settle, like clothing that covers them.
TAB-FULL:v17p466/r1.anchor: فصار لهم سترا يستترون به كما يستترون بالثياب

TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r1.claim: Sleep is rest for the body and quiet for the limbs.
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r1.anchor: كما صحت الرواية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول إذا أصبح وقام من نومه: «الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعدما أماتنا، وإليه النشور»

TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r2.claim: Daytime is waking and life; the word is used of a dead person rising, as in al-A'sha's verse about a dead man who rises.
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r2.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: وجعل النهار يقظة وحياة، من قولهم: نشر الميت، كما قال الأعشى: [البحر السريع]

TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the phrase to mean that people spread out during the day.
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {وجعل النهار نشورا} [الفرقان: 47] قال: ينشر فيه

TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers waking from sleep because it contrasts with sleep at night and sleep resembles death; he concedes Mujahid's spread-for-livelihood reading is plausible, but the root better suggests rising from death or sleep.
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r4.anchor: والذي قاله مجاهد غير بعيد من الصواب

TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites as soundly transmitted the Prophet's morning prayer: praise to God who revived us after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v17p466#2/r5.anchor: كما صحت الرواية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول إذا أصبح وقام من نومه: «الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعدما أماتنا، وإليه النشور»

TABATABAI:25:45-54/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:45-54/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:45-54/r5.claim: Night is a garment because darkness covers people as clothing covers its wearer; sleep is a cessation from work, and daytime is a spreading out to work and seek livelihood, as al-Rāghib explains.
TABATABAI:25:45-54/r5.anchor: كون الليل لباسا إنما هو ستره الإنسان بغشيان الظلمة كما يستر اللباس لابسه

TABATABAI:25:45-54/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:45-54/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:45-54/r6.claim: Night’s covering, sleep’s pause, and the day’s renewed activity parallel the extension of shadow, the sun serving as its guide, and the shadow’s withdrawal.
TABATABAI:25:45-54/r6.anchor: وحال ستره تعالى الناس بلباس الليل وقطعهم به عن العمل والحركة ثم نشرهم للعمل والسعي

TABRISI:25:47-50/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:47-50/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:47-50/r1.claim: The phrase about night as a time of repose is linked to the statement that God made night so people could rest.

TABRISI:25:47-50/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:47-50/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:47-50/r2.claim: Subāt means rest for bodies and a cessation of work.

TABRISI:25:47-50/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:47-50/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:25:47-50/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines subāt as stopping movement while the spirit remains in the body.
TABRISI:25:47-50/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: السبات أن ينقطع عن الحركة والروح

TABRISI:25:47-50/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:47-50/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:47-50/r4.claim: Day is nushūr because the spirit spreads through the body upon waking; the term also recalls resurrection.
TABRISI:25:47-50/r4.anchor: لانتشار الروح باليقظة فيه مأخوذ من نشور البعث

TABRISI:25:47-50/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:47-50/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:25:47-50/r5.claim: Another explanation takes nushūr as people dispersing by day to seek their needs and livelihoods.
TABRISI:25:47-50/r5.anchor: لأن الناس ينتشرون فيه لطلب حوائجهم ومعايشهم فيكون النشور هنا بمعنى التفرق لابتغاء الرزق عن ابن عباس

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r1.claim: The night is called clothing because it covers people.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r1.anchor: جعل لكم الليل لباسا} أي سترا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r2.claim: Subāt means rest; its original sense is stretching out.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r2.anchor: والنوم سباتا} أي راحة. وأصل السبات: التمدد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r3.claim: Nushūr means people spread out or go about during the day.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p313#8/r3.anchor: وجعل النهار نشورا} أي ينتشرون فيه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God clothed them in darkness so they could rest and stop work and movement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ألبسته الظلمة ليسكن فيه. وعلى هذا المعنى: ذا لباس من الظلمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r2.claim: Muqātil glosses the night as rest and links it to the verse about night being made for people to settle in.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني سكنا (¬2). وهو معنى وليس بتفسير، واعتباره بقوله: {هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r3.speaker: أهل العربية والمعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r3.claim: Arabists say darkness is clothing because it covers all people and things, enveloping them like a garment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r3.anchor: وقال أهل العربية، والمعاني: جعل الليل لباسا؛ لأن ظلمته تلبس كل شخص وتغشاه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r4.claim: Dhū al-Rummah's line beginning فلما لبسن الليل is cited as poetic evidence for the clothing image.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r4.anchor: ومن هذا قول ذي الرمة: فلما لبسن الليل (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r5.claim: Al-Layth defines subāt as sleep resembling a swoon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r5.anchor: قال الليث: السبات: السبات: النوم شبه غشية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj says subāt cuts off movement while the spirit remains in the body, making sleep a rest.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: السبات أن يقطع عن الحركة والروح في بدنه: أي: جعلنا نومكم راحة لكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains sleep as a cutting off of people's activities.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say people spread out in the daytime to seek provision.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: ينتشرون فيه لابتغاء الرزق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r9.claim: Nushūr means spreading out and resuming activity; it also names the dead person's renewed life and movement after stillness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r9.anchor: والنشور معناه: التفرق: الانبساط في التصرف، ومنه: نشور الميت، وهو: حياته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r10.claim: Day is called resurrection because night interrupts the sleeper like death and waking brings renewed activity; the verse recalls the blessings of restful sleep and useful daylight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p524/r10.anchor: وحسن ذكر النشور هاهنا؛ لأن النائم بالليل يكون بانقطاعه عن العمل كالميت

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the night is a garment because creation settles and rests in it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r4.anchor: يعني سكنا يسكن فيه الخلق. وهو تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r5.claim: Sleep makes the sleeper inactive and unaware.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r6.claim: Mujahid says people spread out in the daytime to seek their livelihoods.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r6.anchor: تفسير مجاهد: ينتشر فيه الخلق لمعائشهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r7.claim: Qatadah expands the daytime activity to livelihoods, needs, and people's various tasks.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says people disperse during the day seeking provision.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p484/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: {نشورا} [الفرقان: 47] يتفرقون فيه يبتغون الرزق.

ELMALILI:25:47/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:47/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:47/r1.claim: Night is like clothing: the earth's shadow covers people, shields them from the sun's disturbance and others' watchful eyes, and provides conditions for rest.
ELMALILI:25:47/r1.anchor: bedeni örten elbise gibi üzerinize bir örtü yaptı, Güneş’in iz‘âc-ı delâletinden, ağyârın dîde-i si‘âyetinden saklar, istirahatiniz esbâbından birini teşkil eder.

ELMALILI:25:47/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:47/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:47/r2.claim: Subat derives from stopping or suspending activity and can mean rest or death; the rest day is yawm al-sabt, a patient relieved of illness is mesbut, and a dead person is mesbut because life has ceased.
ELMALILI:25:47/r2.anchor: “Sübât” kesmek, ta‘tîl etmek mânasından me’huz olarak rahat ve ölüm mânalarına gelir

ELMALILI:25:47/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:47/r3.speaker: Ebû Müslim
ELMALILI:25:47/r3.claim: Abu Muslim interprets subat as rest.
ELMALILI:25:47/r3.anchor: Ebû Müslim rahat ile tefsir etmiş

ELMALILI:25:47/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:47/r4.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
ELMALILI:25:47/r4.claim: The author reports that the Kashshaf prefers death, since it contrasts with nushur.
ELMALILI:25:47/r4.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf da mevt mânasına olmasını tercih eylemiştir. Çünkü mukabilinde nüşûr geliyor.

ELMALILI:25:47/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:47/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:47/r5.claim: Daytime is a rising into renewed life, figured as resurrection after death: sleepers whose activity stopped at night awaken and begin moving again in the morning.
ELMALILI:25:47/r5.anchor: geceleyin rahat döşeğine yatıp ta‘tîl-i faaliyet ederek

ELMALILI:25:47/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:47/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:47/r6.claim: Those who do not hope for resurrection do not desire this renewed life.
ELMALILI:25:47/r6.anchor: Bu nüşûru ummayanlar o hayâtı arzu etmeyenlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:45/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:45/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:45/r1.claim: After condemning those who deify their desires and abandon reason, the passage appeals to human reason and insight, using nature's order and divine laws to invite faith in God and guidance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:45/r1.anchor: insanın aklına, irfanına ve basiretine hitap eden deliller ortaya konmakta

NAHHAS:v3p163/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p163/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p163/r2.claim: The verb جعل has two objects; سباتا means rest. Repeating جعل reinforces the construction, though والنهار نشورا would also be possible outside the Qurʾānic wording.
NAHHAS:v3p163/r2.anchor: و سبات بمعنى الراحة وأعاد جعل توكيدا ولو كان والنهار نشورا لجاز في غير القرآن

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r1.claim: Jurjani points to the delicate effect of deletion and indefiniteness in the poetic phrase about a gaze and greetings along the road.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r1.anchor: وعرف لطف موقع الحذف والتنكير في قوله :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r2.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r2.claim: The phrase لي عليك دموع has an almost magical effect because لي precedes عليك and دموع is indefinite.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r2.anchor: وما في قول البحتري : ' لي عليك دموع ' من شبه السحر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r3.claim: He praises the line about stars rising auspiciously for its nobility, elevated level, and fine craftsmanship.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r3.anchor: وعرف كذلك شرف قوله : ( وقالت نجوم لو طلعن بأسعد )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r4.claim: Sensitivity to these literary distinctions is rare among people.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r4.anchor: والبلاء ، والداء العياء أن هذا الإحساس قليل في الناس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r5.claim: A writer may produce a well-placed distinction in poetry or prose without knowing that he has succeeded, while remaining able to miss his own failures.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r5.anchor: حتى إنه ليكون أن يقع للرجل الشيء من هذه الفروق والوجوه في شعر يقوله

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r6.claim: Only a person with responsive taste and a perceptive heart can be shown these subtleties; trying to explain them to someone who cannot see them is futile.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r6.anchor: حتى تظفر بمن له طبع إذا قدحته ورى ، وقلب إذا أريته رأى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r7.claim: The danger is an ungifted person who believes himself qualified to judge and speaks foolishly; someone aware of his limits is rational and does not exceed them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p395/r7.anchor: إذا ظن العادم لها أنه أوتيها ، وأنه ممن يكمل للحكم

TABRISI:25:41-42/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:41-42/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:41-42/r14.claim: Subāt means cessation of work: one may say “he shaved his head,” and Saturday is named as the day work ceased.
TABRISI:25:41-42/r14.anchor: والسبات قطع العمل ومنه سبت رأسه سبتا إذا حلقه ومنه يوم السبت وهو يوم قطع العمل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p93/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p93/r3.claim: Calling night a garment means that it covers and screens the eyes; Dhu al-Rumma’s image of night dyeing the stones shows darkness as a covering.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p93/r3.anchor: قال ذو الرمة : ودويه مثل السماء اعتسفتها

JISHUMI:v7p5304/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r4.claim: The root of sabt is cutting: subāt stops work, shaving cuts hair, and the Sabbath is the day work stops.
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r4.anchor: والسبت: أصله القطع، والسبات: قطع العمل، وسبت رأسه: حلقه، ويوم السبت: يوم قطع العمل

JISHUMI:v7p5304/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r5.claim: Nashr is the opposite of folding and means spreading; it is also used of the dead being raised and rising.
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r5.anchor: والنشر: خلاف الطي، وهو الانبساط، ومنه: أنشر الله الموتى فنشروا

JISHUMI:v7p5304/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r6.speaker: الأعشى
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r6.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s poem calls a dead person الناشر, using the word for one who rises.
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r6.anchor: قال الأعشى: حتى يقول الناس مما رأوا ... يا عجبا للميت الناشر

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r32.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r32.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r32.claim: Night is like clothing because its darkness conceals everything and provides rest.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r32.anchor: أي: سترا تستترون به وتسكنون فيه، وشبه الليل باللباس؛ لأنه يستر كل شيء بظلمته

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r33.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r33.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r33.claim: Another explanation compares night to clothing because people wear undergarments and outer garments when sleeping.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r33.anchor: وقيل: لأن الناس يلبسون الدثار والشعار عند النوم

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r34.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r34.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r34.claim: Sleep is bodily rest and cessation from work.

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r35.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r35.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r35.claim: Day is when people spread out to earn a living and pursue activities.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r35.anchor: وجعل النهار نشورا أي: تنتشرون فيه لطلب المعاش، وتنبسطون في التصرفات

JISHUMI:v7p5310/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r5.claim: The surface wording suggests sleep is a distinct entity or meaning.
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r5.anchor: ويدل ظاهر قوله: (والنوم سباتا) أن النوم معنى

JISHUMI:v7p5310/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r6.speaker: أكثر مشايخنا
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r6.claim: Most of the author’s teachers deny sleep is an entity in itself; they describe it as forgetfulness and torpor, to which rest is attached.
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r6.anchor: وأكثر مشايخنا على أنه ليس بمعنى برأسه، وإنما هو سهو وفتور فعلق الراحة بذلك
